description: U.S. Climate Extremes Index is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. The U.S. Climate Extremes Index documents the area of the contiguous United States that experienced extreme conditions during various time periods. The index is calculated as the arithmetic average of values from a specified set of extreme events, weighted by the percent area that experienced the defined conditions. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds. Assets: Critical Facilities, Cultural and Community Services, Energy and Utilities, People. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
